New: Choose channels (keep, drop, reorder, recolour and rename channels; pixels copied exactly). Read image reads WebP, AVIF and JPEG 2000 and records whether the file is lossless, lossy or may be lossy, warning when pixels are lossy. A single coloured channel is drawn in its colour in every picture. Needs Rill 0.4.0.

rill.image 0.3.0 (a new line; D119, D120)

- Scale bar: drag the bar on the node's Draw tab; it settles in the nearest corner. Drag its end to change the length, which snaps to 1, 2 or 5 x 10^n um. Settings have clearer names and groups; saved values load unchanged and draw the same pixels.
- Split channels: new Outputs choice. Separate works as before; List gives one list of every channel, so the next nodes run once per channel. Use {index} in Save image's filename to save each channel to its own file.
- Split channels now keeps the name of a channel that has no colour (it used to become "Channel N"). Measurement columns built from merged channels can therefore be named, for example, "DAPI" instead of "Channel 1".
- Saved nodes on the 0.2 line keep running on 0.2 if it is installed; use Update or "Update all plugin nodes" to move them to 0.3.

rill.image 0.4.0 (a new line; needs Rill 0.4.1; D126, D127)

- Save image: RGB and multi-channel images save as the composite a result preview shows (each channel in its colour). One channel still saves exactly, and TIFFs keep the micrometre calibration.
- Draw shape: the drawing view now matches the output picture (line widths, arrow heads, dashes, labels).
- Draw shape: new Text tool. Text and labels use bundled Noto Sans and Noto Sans TC (SIL Open Font License), so Greek, symbols such as um and x, and Chinese draw correctly.
- Draw shape: new Contrast setting (As recorded / Auto); the drawing view follows it.
- Labels on existing drawings change font to Noto Sans, so use Update to move saved nodes to 0.4.

rill.image 0.4.1 (a fix on the 0.4 line)

- Number fields in the image editors (Draw shape's style fields, rule values, toggle min/max, threshold, kernel cells) keep focus while the node re-runs, so holding an arrow key or a spin arrow keeps stepping the value. A held Draw shape field is one undo step.
- Nothing a saved workflow produces changes. Works best with Rill 0.4.2; on 0.4.1 the fields behave as before.

FRAP: Read time-lapse (a whole .oir or TIFF time-lapse as one item, previewed with Play), FRAP regions, FRAP normalize; Save time-lapse (ImageJ TIFF or GIF) and readers that name the reader a file needs. FRAP regions and ROI mask draw with one region editor: each region a curve plus brushed minus erased pixels, with pen (⌥-click corners), ellipse, rectangle, lasso, brush and eraser that change the region, Select to resize and rotate; regions saved by earlier versions convert with the same pixels. Traditional Chinese (zh-TW) labels; search keywords and built-in tags.

rill.image 0.11.1 (since 0.8.0):
- The time-lapse and FRAP nodes moved to the new rill.video plugin (D195).
- Split channels matches channels by capture (laser and emission): a port per ticked channel, inactive when a file lacks it, or a List named by your own names (D196).
- FRAP reference leaves out the bleached region; XY line Overlay and Mark (D178, D181).
- The Scale bar's drawing is shared with rill.video's video overlays; its output is unchanged (D197).
First release on the plugin channel.
Native code now ships with the plugin.
Its node UI now ships with the plugin instead of Rill's core (D106), so UI fixes arrive as plugin releases. Needs Rill 0.3.0.

New: Compose figure (arrange charts, images and figures on a page in Focus; D101-D103), Compress image (small palette PNGs at a print size), Read figure (SVG, PNG, TIFF, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, JPEG 2000). Save figure takes a chart directly: the file extension is the format, with its own DPI. Rendered captions show file size. Needs Rill 0.4.0.

Compose figure: text, lines, arrows, rectangles and ellipses on the page; A B C panel letters with Relabel; local chart edits (double-click a chart panel to restyle it for this figure only). Items keep their place in points; anything cut at or off the page edge is warned about. Edit figure: text items gain a Weight control. Needs Rill 0.4.0.

rill.plot 0.3.1 (a fix on the 0.3 line; D113, D120)

- Compose figure: double-click an SVG panel in Focus to touch it up. Hide elements (matplotlib's stray white boxes, for example), change fill and stroke colour, stroke width and opacity, edit real text (words, size, bold, italic), and move elements by dragging or with the arrow keys. A breadcrumb and an element list reach groups and hidden elements.
- Touch-ups are stored in the panel and follow elements by their SVG id, so re-exporting the SVG from Inkscape keeps them; an edit whose element is gone is listed as no longer matching. The SVG file itself is never changed.
- An SVG panel's Crop is now a button in the panel tools; image panels keep double-click crop.
- Saved workflows pick this up on their next run; nothing they already produce changes.

rill.plot 0.3.2 (a fix on the 0.3 line; D137)

- Axis tick Step: in Edit figure (and Compose figure's chart edits), set Step next to Decimals on the X or Y tick labels to space ticks at whole multiples, for example 0, 5, 10, 15 on a 0-30 axis. Empty keeps automatic ticks.
- Labels take the decimals the step needs; Decimals still wins. A step that would draw more than 200 ticks falls back to automatic ticks with a warning.
- Log, category and heatmap-row axes, pair plots and angle charts ignore the step with a warning.
- Saved figures look the same unless a step is set.

Traditional Chinese (zh-TW) labels and figure editor messages (English where the host has no translations); search keywords and built-in tags. A refused table input names the setting to change and the text that is not a number.

Figures in Reports: the plugin offers its chart layout and figure layout maths to Rill's report editor (figureServices). XY line overlay and marks (off by default); figure facts for Results. Saved workflows on 0.3 stay on 0.3 until updated.
The Sequence viewer ships as this plugin's own UI. Its alignment figure needs Rill with the own-environment renderer fix (main 2d72b28).
Sequence viewer drags (selection, names, labels, list rows, pan) follow the viewer when it redraws mid-drag (D109).

versions.notes: First release: smarter search for Rill itself (the Manual, the workflow library). Finds what you mean even in other words or the other language. Optional; about 160 MB; Mac (Apple Silicon) only for now.

rill.video 0.3.0, first release:
- The time-lapse and FRAP nodes, moved from rill.image (D195).
- Read time-lapse reads every channel; Split channels picks them by capture (D196).
- Save time-lapse writes MP4 (H.264, encoded in pure Rust) for PowerPoint and QuickTime, with a time stamp (zero at the bleach or the first frame) and a scale bar, both draggable in the preview; frames per second or real time (D197).

The former `rill-align` sample plugin, renamed and grown into Rill's sequence plugin. It is a clean break: workflows
saved with `rill-align`'s nodes (`align.read`, `align.kalign`, `align.save`) are not migrated; their nodes are now
`sequence.read`, `sequence.align` and `sequence.save`. The Sequence viewer (`plot.alignment`) keeps its id.

- Read sequences reads a plain text file (a Sanger read) as one sequence named after the file; one sequence per line
  is the explicit format "lines".
- Sequence sets may carry a type per row; Align refuses a set of mixed types, and a name with two sequences, naming them.
- New: Sequences (a typed or pasted reference library and collector) and Sequence selection (the wanted stretch of a
  read, matched against the references by rill_sequence_native).
- Sequence selection writes its proposal and every candidate (identity, coverage, rank, which was proposed) to its outputs
  (`Match`, `Candidates`), so review shows what the node proposed and the run record says why a reference was picked.
- A held review choice that no longer matches the read, the references or the Output (or is off the codons of its frame
  when the output is protein) refuses the item in words; it is never replaced by the proposal. When no reference is clearly
  ahead the best match's stretch is proposed, with the reference left unpicked.
- Read sequences types each record by its letters: a file mixing DNA and protein is a mixed set with a type per row.
